chunk_findings.detail: The manifest lists `tests/test_mcp_families.py` as modified (`+7 -1`), but the stated acceptance criterion explicitly requires this budget test file to have no diff (`git diff shows no edit to those test files`) so that the unchanged 59,000 limit is actually being exercised. Any edit to this file can change the measured surface, the comparison baseline, or the effective ceiling, so the test passing after the edit is not evidence that the original budget constraint still passes.
chunk_findings.title: test_the_whole_families_surface_is_much_smaller_than_the_flat_one

chunk_findings.detail: The change alters the advertised MCP tool surface (`all` now excludes the rare tools and `full` is added), but the manifest contains no golden tools snapshot update among the eight changed files. `tests/golden/test_golden_mcp_tools.py` is required to pass and compares the generated tools/list surface to a golden artifact; with the golden artifact unchanged, the golden test will fail against the new tool list. The acceptance also says the golden tools snapshot is regenerated through `ddflow pins regenerate`, so its absence makes the change incomplete.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/test_golden_mcp_tools.py

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest shows `tests/test_mcp_families.py` is modified (`+7 -1`), but the stated acceptance condition for this change is that the two budget test files (`tests/test_mcp_families.py` and `tests/test_session_start_budget.py`) must have no edits in the diff, with limits unchanged. Therefore, under the required acceptance/CI check, this change is wrong: even if the test passes, the diff violates the explicit constraint that the red budget test file not be edited.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py

chunk_findings.detail: The patch edits one of the two budget tests that the stated acceptance criterion says must not be edited. The hunk changes the union calculation used by `test_the_whole_families_surface_is_much_smaller_than_the_flat_one` from counting every member-tool property to filtering out properties for which `FS.unlisted_arg` returns true. Because `tests/test_mcp_rare_tools.py` asserts that every optional argument of a rare tool is unlisted, this removes those optional argument names from the measured family surface. For example, if a family member such as `ddflow_lesson_show` has an optional `id` argument, the old test counted `id` in the family surface and the new test omits it, directly reducing the measured surface that was only 644 bytes/tokens over the 59,000 limit. That makes the budget test pass by narrowing the assertion rather than proving the production surface moved enough, violating the operator decision and the explicit “git diff shows no edit to those test files” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py:54

chunk_findings.detail: The change edits one of the two budget test files that the acceptance criteria explicitly require to remain untouched (`git diff shows no edit to those test files`). The manifest shows `tests/test_mcp_families.py (+7 -1)`, the file containing `test_the_whole_families_surface_is_much_smaller_than_the_flat_one`. Even if the edit only adds an import or helper, it violates the operator decision that the red budget test must be fixed by moving tools out of the default surface, not by changing the budget-test file; if the edit altered the expected surface calculation or assertions, it could make the budget test pass without actually fixing the start cost.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts the default `all` tier behavior (`_list(repo) == expected` excluding `RARE_TOOLS`) without first clearing `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`. If the test process has `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=full` (or any non-default tier) in its environment, the first `_list(repo)` call returns the env-selected list rather than the default list, so the byte/list comparison fails even though the implementation’s default tier is correct. The same file’s unknown-tier test explicitly calls `monkeypatch.delenv("DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS", raising=False)` for this reason, indicating the env knob is not otherwise isolated here.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py::test_all_is_the_unfiltered_list_less_the_rare_tools_and_full_is_all_of_it

chunk_findings.detail: In `tests/test_mcp_rare_tools.py`, line 48 passes `{"_probe": 1}` in `arguments` when calling `tools/call`, but some tools may not accept unexpected keyword arguments or schema validation will reject `_probe`. Given an input where the rare tool's argument schema strictly forbids unknown properties, `tools/call` returns an error response, causing `assert "unknown tool" not in text.lower()` to pass vacuously while the actual call failed due to the probe argument.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_rare_tools.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest lists `tests/test_mcp_families.py` as modified (`+7 -1`), but the acceptance criterion explicitly says the budget tests must pass with limits unchanged and that `git diff` shows **no edit** to `tests/test_mcp_families.py` or `tests/test_session_start_budget.py`. Any diff to `tests/test_mcp_families.py` violates that condition. Since this file contains `test_the_whole_families_surface_is_much_smaller_than_the_flat_one`, modifying it risks changing the measured surface or expectations instead of proving that moving tools out of the default advertised list fixes the budget failure.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py

chunk_findings.detail: The change claims rare tools are “not listed in its family's `action` enum and description,” but the implementation only suppresses optional non-`action` arguments. `_union` still loops over every family member and, for `arg == ACTION`, unconditionally adds the member’s action name/description into the family schema’s operation/action property; `unlisted_arg` explicitly never skips `ACTION`. Thus, for any family that contains a rare tool such as `ddflow_hooks`, the generated family tool still advertises `hooks` in its action/op description, so the tool is still part of the advertised family surface and the `profile_note` wording that such tools are “NOT in `tools/list`” is false for the family listing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/tools/family_schema.py:_union / ddflow/surfaces/tools/rare.py:RARE_TOOLS

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance explicitly says the two red budget tests must pass with the limits unchanged and with `git diff` showing no edit to those test files. This diff edits `tests/test_mcp_families.py` and changes the test’s union calculation to filter out rare-tool optional arguments via `FS.unlisted_arg`. That means the families budget test can pass because the test itself now ignores part of the family surface, not solely because the tools were moved out of the default list; it violates the operator decision that the fix must not edit the budget test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_families.py:54

chunk_findings.detail: This test does not actually prove the moved tools are callable by family action. If `FS.route(...)` returns a string error that does not contain the exact lowercase substring `"unknown action"`—for example `"missing required argument"` or `"Unknown action"` with capital U—the first assertion passes and the subsequent `if not isinstance(routed, str):` block is skipped, so the test never checks that `routed.tool == tool`. The RPC check is similarly permissive: it only asserts the text does not contain `"unknown tool"`, so a response such as `"ddflow_wait is not available"` would pass even though the rare tool is not callable under the `all` tier.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_rare_tools.py::test_a_rare_tool_stays_callable_by_name_and_by_family_action

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts the default/`all` surface before clearing `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`, but the same file explicitly treats that environment variable as an override (`test_unknown_tier_is_refused_on_write_but_lists_everything_at_start` deletes it before checking the file-backed tier). If the test process has `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=full`, the first `_list(repo)` call returns the full list including every tool in `RARE_TOOLS`, while `expected` filters those names out; the `json.dumps(_list(repo)) == json.dumps(expected)` assertion then fails even though the implementation is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py::test_all_is_the_unfiltered_list_less_the_rare_tools_and_full_is_all_of_it

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `ddflow_help` with whatever ambient `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` is present before asserting that the help text mentions the `all` tier and all rare tool names. If the environment has `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=full`, the first help call is the full-tier help, which by the test’s own later expectation says nothing about tool tiers, so `"`all` tool tier" in text` fails. The test should `monkeypatch.delenv("DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS", raising=False)` before the first help call.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_tiers.py::test_help_names_what_the_all_tier_leaves_out_and_full_says_nothing
